narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed carefully, and unfortunately, we were unable to approve it at this time. The decision was based on several key factors in your financial profile that suggested a higher risk of difficulty repaying the loan. Specifically, the model estimated an 86% probability that this loan could present challenges, which is why we had to deny the request.

One of the most significant concerns was the status of your checking account. Having a negative balance or no checking account at all is uncommon among approved applicants—most have at least some funds available, and nearly half maintain a balance of 200 DM or more. This raised a red flag, as it may indicate limited financial flexibility to handle additional debt. Your credit history, while strong in the sense that all past obligations at this bank were paid, was also unusual—only about 3% of approved applicants had a similar history, which made it harder for the model to assess your reliability compared to those with more typical payment patterns.

Another factor that worked against your application was the lack of clear property ownership. Most approved applicants either own real estate, have a car or other assets, or hold a life insurance policy—something that provides security for the bank. Since your profile didn’t show any of these, it made the loan appear riskier. On the positive side, your employment duration of 4-7 years and the fact that you’ve been at your current residence for four years were favorable signs, as stability in these areas is generally a good indicator of creditworthiness.

The amount you requested—1,442 DM—was well below the average loan size of nearly 2,900 DM, which might have been a point in your favor. However, the combination of your checking account status, credit history, and lack of property outweighed this. Additionally, while your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is manageable, it’s slightly higher than the average for approved applicants, which may have also contributed to the decision.

To improve your chances in the future, you might consider building a positive balance in your checking account, even if it’s small, as this would address one of the biggest concerns in your application. If possible, establishing some form of property or savings—even modestly—could also help demonstrate financial stability. Since your credit history is otherwise strong, taking steps to align more closely with the profiles of approved applicants could make a meaningful difference. We encourage you to review these areas and reapply when your situation has improved.
